method: independent re-derivation from the definitions; every load-bearing constant recomputed, then attacked by parameter-space search for a counterexample to each printed step. Scripts: REFEREE3_check.py, REFEREE3_check2.py, REFEREE3_check3.py.

G-a.exactness_claim: correct - unit-step transversal coordinate + discrete IVT gives a vertex at level exactly ceil(D); subpath optimality gives the through-vertex inequality with no seam and no O(b)
corrections: site count N <= 2(rho r + 1) <= 4 rho r, not 6 rho r (B5)
union's far-longitudinal sites are not priced by the hypothesis as literally stated (B1)

G-b(i).note: D <= r(b-a_w)/(2 a_w) re-derived exactly; U[1,2] cap r/2 matches bandcap_check.py; the machine check is a valid bug-catcher for the deterministic cap and nothing more
corrections: state a_w > 0 as a hypothesis: the lemma is uniformly elliptic, not merely bounded-weight (B10 i)
the cap generalises to arbitrary pairs; G-f needs that form and does not state it (A1b)

G-b(ii).conditional_on: how (H-curv-LOWER) is read for displaced points off the segment
G-b(ii).detail: (P-conc) direction-uniformity is CORRECT as published - steep legs are free. The second half ('the displaced point v is arbitrary at its distance in the condition as stated') is a reading, not an argument, and it is load-bearing: it is exactly what the far-longitudinal sites of the G-a union need. FREE for axis-aligned spans (implied by the midpoint case, proved in B1 fallback (a), 0 numerical violations). NOT free for tilted spans, which v2 consumes.
G-b(ii).repair_preferred: add the longitudinal-overshoot clause (B1): excess >= g(e_2) * overshoot by convexity alone, so far sites cost exp(-c1 g(e_2) delta sqrt(r)/(6 sqrt(2+rho))) and the union restricts to j in [-delta r/2, r + delta r/2], inside the window as written. No constant loss.
G-b(ii).repair_fallback: keep the offset reading and pay c_- -> c_-/(2+b/a_w) at the far sites

confirmed: three-way split with Delta = c_- Dbar^2/r - C3 sqrt(r) log r
normalisation uniformity: all pair lengths in [Dbar, (2 + b/a_w) r]
U[1,2] instantiation c'' = c1/12, Form B c1/24 -- CORRECT
the wlog delta <= min(1, 3C2/c_-) does imply BOTH (P-conc) range checks, span and short leg; the iter-114 correction of the first print is right
the mid-band containment in through-level-ceil(delta r)

corrections.Form_A_prefactor: 12 C1 (b/a_w) r  (was 18 C1 (b/a_w) r); one-sided G-e: 6 C1 (b/a_w) r
corrections.C_triple_prime: delta^2/4  (was delta^2) - ceiling-safe for r >= 2/delta; equivalently read the window as ceil(D) <= delta r
corrections.new_wlog: c1 <= 3 sqrt(2 + b/a_w)/C3, i.e. c'' <= 1/(2 C3) - closes an unproved middle band of sigma (45 of 324 gridded points had one) and makes the consumer's A >= C3 c'' branch vacuous
corrections.nonempty_range: the statement must carry r >= r_0 with delta^2 sqrt(r) >= max((2C3/c_-) log r, (2/(c'' c_-)) log(12 C1 (b/a_w) r)); measured r_0 ranges 1e5.5 to 1e14 over plausible constants, and 1488 of 2187 gridded points had an EMPTY range at r <= 1e10

G-d.note: no consumption site needing a confined-geodesic wandering tail was found in this round; revival clause not triggered; the iter-116 correction to the H-version parenthesis is right

G-e.note: nothing else silently used the two-sided form - the band cap only counts sites, the normalisations use |Dbar|, the split is sign-agnostic
G-e.correction: one-sided prefactor 6 C1 (b/a_w) r under the sharper count

G-f(i).verdict: CONFIRMED in total, DEFECT in justification + one omission
G-f(i).confirmed: the containment over boundary pairs is right and needs no conditioning and no independence (subpath optimality + union bound); the o(1) arithmetic given the count is right
G-f(i).defect_1: the per-boundary site count names the wrong scale. The band cap at slab scale bounds a piece's excursion relative to its own endpoints, not the location of those endpoints; the only deterministic confinement is the TOP-scale cap, C M n per boundary. The printed total C' M n^3 nevertheless stands, because M is a fixed constant and C' swallows M^3 - which should be said, and 'at slab scale n' should be struck.
G-f(i).defect_2: the union omits same-boundary excursion pieces (a geodesic may enter and leave a slab through one boundary). Their chords are horizontal - outside any arc around e_2 - so the lemma cannot price them at any threshold.
G-f(i).repair_1: state (i) on the complement of (ii)'s event {global deviation >= theta n/2}: then every crossing point has |h| < theta n/2, sites per boundary <= theta n + 1, total ~ C M theta^2 n^3, and the printed shape and the log-quantile cost stand
G-f(i).repair_2: same-boundary pieces are controlled deterministically by the generalised band cap: excursion <= (b-a_w)|u-v|_1/(2 a_w). No probabilistic input needed.
G-f(i).severity: presentational for the total; the omission in defect_2 is substantive

G-f(ii).verdict: CONFIRMED in shape, DEFECT(arithmetic) in two side-claims
confirmed: the inclusion |h2-h1| <= |h1|+|h2| => max >= theta n/2 => contained in a top-scale deviation event with axis-aligned endpoints
the range identity: sigma^2 <= delta^2 sqrt(R) is EXACTLY D <= delta R for D = sigma R^{3/4} (checked to 12 digits)
the draft's worked point (M=5, theta=0.05, n=1e4 -> exponent 0.0056) reproduces exactly, and the small-n regime IS honestly excluded
G-f(ii).defect_a: 'true for every theta below the band cap at any M >= 5' is an over-claim: the condition is theta <= 2 delta M, which fails when delta < theta/(2M) (e.g. delta=0.01, theta=0.2, M=5). The gridded check is delta-blind (delta = 1 implicitly). In the regime that matters - theta = the o(1) arc half-width - it holds.
G-f(ii).defect_b: the threshold n >~ M^3/theta^4 omits the union's logarithm and 1/(c'' c_-)^2. Corrected: n_0 = (16/(c'' c_-)^2) (M^3/theta^4) log^2(C M n). Measured: M=8, theta=0.05, c''c_- = 1 gives n_0 ~ 1e12.5 against the draft's 8.2e7; at c''c_- = 0.01, n_0 ~ 1e16.5.
G-f(ii).unstated_c: G-f(i)'s own 'far inside the range' has a threshold too: (log M + 3 log n)/(c'' c_-) <= delta^2 sqrt(n); at c''c_- = 0.01, delta = 0.1 that is n >= 1e12

seam_V5-1.note: A >= C3 c'' is exactly the condition that sigma^2 = 2A log l/(c'' c_-) dominate (2C3/c_-) log r' at r' <= l; the A >= 2 branch covers the second threshold. B3's wlog makes the C3 c'' branch vacuous, so A = 2 suffices.

seam_V5-2.detail: 'sigma^2 = Theta(log l) inside delta^2 sqrt(r') for l large, ANY fixed delta - no window condition survives' is asymptotically true with an unstated and unfree threshold. Written out: l^{cb/2}/log l >= 2 A sqrt(K)/(delta^2 c'' c_-), cb <= 0.12 the base-scale exponent.
seam_V5-2.consequence: the package's operative threshold is max(l_0, l_1) with l_0 ~ 1e80; for plausible U[1,2] constants (c''c_- = c1 c_-/12 ~ 0.01) l_1 is the binding one, at 1e127

notation.detail: v2 section 2 uses c for two different constants in adjacent lines: (H-wand)'s tail constant in sigma := (A log l/c)^{1/theta}, and the base-scale exponent in r' >= l^c/K

corrected_constants_deliverable.c'': c1/(6 sqrt(2 + b/a_w))  -- UNCHANGED, confirmed; U[1,2]: c1/12
corrected_constants_deliverable.Form_A: P(dev >= sigma W_r) <= 12 C1 (b/a_w) r [ exp(-c'' c_- sigma^2) + exp(-c1 g(e_2) delta sqrt(r)/(6 sqrt(2+b/a_w))) ]
corrected_constants_deliverable.Form_A_one_sided: 6 C1 (b/a_w) r x the same bracket
corrected_constants_deliverable.Form_B: P <= exp(-(c''/2) c_- sigma^2) once sigma^2 >= (2/(c'' c_-)) log(12 C1 (b/a_w) r)
corrected_constants_deliverable.r_0_NEW: delta^2 sqrt(r) >= max((2 C3/c_-) log r, (2/(c'' c_-)) log(12 C1 (b/a_w) r))
corrected_constants_deliverable.seam_wiring: theta = 2, C = 1, c = (c''/2) c_- = c1 c_-/(12 sqrt(2 + b/a_w)) -- unchanged IF the overshoot clause is adopted; c1 c_-/(12 (2+b/a_w)^{3/2}) (U[1,2]: c1 c_-/96) if the offset reading is paid for instead
corrected_constants_deliverable.seam_l_1_NEW: l^{cb/2}/log l >= 2 A sqrt(K)/(delta^2 c'' c_-)

overall: The mathematics holds. Every load-bearing step I re-derived independently came out as printed, including the whole of G-c. What does not hold is the range bookkeeping: 'polylog, well inside the range' is treated as free in four places (G-c's own range, G-f(i), G-f(ii), and the seam) and in each the threshold is a real, computable, large number - one of which (l_1 >= 1e127 for plausible constants) sits above the 1e80 the v2 document already apologises for. Recommend: MAJOR REVISION of the range ledger, MINOR REVISION of the constants (all listed above), and one new free clause (longitudinal overshoot) that closes the only genuine hole in the union.
repair_interaction_B11: B3's wlog c1 <= 3 sqrt(2+b/a_w)/C3 forces c'' c_- <= c_-/(2 C3), and B8's seam threshold scales as 1/(delta^2 c'' c_-), so closing the middle band RAISES l_1: at C3 = 2, c_- = 0.2, delta = 1 it gives l_1 ~ 1e78, and at delta = 0.1, l_1 > 1e109. Price the two repairs together.
